<head-word>סְטַרְנַלְיָיה</head-word>
<pos> f.</pos>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition> (Saturnalia) 
<italic>the Saturnalia</italic>, a Roman festival beginning on the 17
<sup>th</sup> of December and lasting several days.</definition>
<notes> Ab. Zar. I, 3 Y. ed. (Mish. a. 
<pgbrk id="pg974" />Bab. ed. 8
<sup>a</sup> variously corrupted or perverted). Y. ib. 39
<sup>c</sup> (cacophemistic etymology) שׁנאה טֹמונה שׁונא נוקם ונ̇וט̇ר̇ hatred hidden (under the merriment of social equality and good will), he (the Roman) hates &c. Ib. ס' דביישן the Saturnalian fair of Scythopolis (v. בֵּישָׁן). Ib. top ס' אינה אסורה וכ' during the Saturnalia trading is forbidden only with those who worship thereon (celebrate it). Bab. ib. 8
<sup>a</sup> ס' שמונה ימים לפני וכ' the Saturnalia begin eight days before the solstice; Y. l. c. ס' לאחר וכ' (corr. acc.). Deut. R. s. 7 סטרגלים, סטרנלים (corr. acc.).</notes></sense></senses></entry>

<entry id="O00549">
<head-word>סִיג</head-word>
<hw-number>I</hw-number>
<pos> m.</pos>
<language-key>(b. h.;</language-key>
<language-reference>
<xref rid="A00083"> סוּג)</xref></language-reference>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition> [
<italic>that which is to be removed;</italic> cmp. בְּדִיל,] 
<italic>dross, base metal; refuse</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Bekh. 51
<sup>a</sup> שלא יביא ס' לעזרה Ar. (ed. סִיגָה) in order that one may not bring base metal to the Temple (therefore stamped silver coins had to be brought along; Rashi: סיגה וכסף סיגים base metal or non-purified silver).—
<plural-form>Pl. סִיגִים, סִגִּים</plural-form>. Num. R. s. 14 (ref. to סוג לב, Prov. XIV, 14) אותו הלב שהוא מלא ס' וכ' the heart full of base things, will get sick of its own ways. Ib. s. 13 יחזקאל קורא אותם ס' Ezekiel calls them base metal (ref. to Ez. XXII, 18). Midr. Till. to Ps. CXIX, 119) אכל הענבים נעשה ס' ed. Bub. (ed. עושה סוגים, corr. acc.) after he has eaten the grapes, it (the cluster) becomes refuse.</notes></sense></senses></entry>

<italic>luxuriant growth</italic> (in good or bad sense).</definition>
<notes> Tosef. Ukts. I, 2 (T’bul Yom III) הס' של אשכלות the foliage covering the clusters of grapes, של רצפות the cobweb-like covering of fruits; Ukts. I, 2.—
<plural-form>Pl. סִיגִּים, סִגִּים</plural-form>. Deut. R. s. 3 (ref. to Deut. VII, 13) מה פרי אדמתך ס' וכ' as the fruit of thy ground will be of luxuriant growth, so will be the fruit of thy womb (strong people). Num. R. s. 16; Tanḥ. Sh’laḥ 12 (ref. to Is.XVII, 1</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>1)</number>
<definition />
<notes> ביום שאמר … (נ) עשיתם ס' on the day that he intended to plant you in the land, you became a luxuriant growth (degenerated); Num. R. s. 7.—[Sifra Sh’mini, ch. VII, Par. 6, v.

<entry id="O00710">
<head-word>סִימָן</head-word>
<pos> m.</pos>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition> (סוּם I, v. 
<xref rid="O00337">סוּמָא II</xref>) 
<italic>mark, sign; omen; symptom; cipher, mnemotechnical note</italic>.</definition>
<notes> B. Mets. 22
<sup>b</sup> ס' העשוי לידרס לא הוי ס' a mark (on a lost object) which is liable to be effaced by treading upon it, is no mark (by which one can claim it). Ib. 23
<sup>a</sup> ס' הבא מאליו an accidental mark (not made purposely). Ib. 24
<sup>b</sup> נתן בה ס' he told a sign (by which he identified it). Ib. 27
<sup>b</sup> ס' מובהק a distinguished (specific) mark of identification.—Ber. 24
<sup>b</sup> ס' יפה an auspicious omen. Taan. 30
<sup>b</sup> אינו רואה סִימַן ברכה וכ' will never see a sign of blessing (will labor without success).—Kidd. 16
<sup>b</sup> דברי הכל ס' all agree that it is a sign of puberty. Ḥull. 61
<sup>a</sup> עוף הבא בס' אחד a bird which has one of the four marks of cleanness. Erub. 54
<sup>b</sup> (ref. to שימה, Deut. XXXI, 19) א"ת שימה אלא סִימָנָהּ read not 
<italic>simah</italic> (put it), but 
<italic>simanah</italic> (its mark, catchwords). Ib. 54
<sup>a</sup>, a. fr. (editorial gloss) ס' וכ' the catchwords for the subject following are &c.; a. v. fr.—Trnsf. 
<italic>the organ, the cutting of which is an indication that the animal has been slaughtered according to the ritual, the windpipe</italic> and 
<italic>the gullet</italic>. Ḥull. 27
<sup>b</sup> הכשרו בס' אחד is made ritually fit for eating by the cutting of either of the organs; a. fr.—
<plural-form>Pl. סִימָנִים, סִימָנִין</plural-form>. B. Mets. 27
<sup>a</sup>, a. fr. ס' דאורייתא וכ' is identification by marks a Biblical or a rabbinical institution? Ib. II, 5 שיש בה ס' which can be identified by signs. Ib. 7 אמר אבידה ולא אמר סִימָנֶיהָ if he states the object he has lost, but cannot describe it.—Kidd. 4
<sup>a</sup>, a. fr. סִימָנֵי נערות evidences of puberty (v. נַעֲרוּת). Ib. 16
<sup>a</sup> קונה את עצמה בס' acquires herself (becomes free) on showing evidences of puberty. Ib.
<sup>b</sup> אין ס' באיש a man-servant does not go out free on reaching puberty. Ḥull.III, 6 סימני בהמה וכ' the distinguishing marks of cleanness in animals &c. Ib. 27
<sup>b</sup> לחייבו בשני ס' to make it obligatory to cut both organs (the windpipe and the gullet). Ib. 44
<sup>a</sup> עיקור ס' the case of the organs’ being torn loose before cutting. Erub. 54
<sup>b</sup> אין התורה … בס' knowledge of the Law can be obtained only by means of signs (rubrication by catchwords). Ib. 21
<sup>b</sup> סימני טעמים notes of accentuation (v. טַעַם); a. fr.</notes></sense></senses></entry>
